title: Mozzarella di Bufala con Prosciutto
subtitle: Buffalo mozzarella with prosciutto crudo and extra-virgin olive oil
excerpt: Mozzarella di bufala con prosciutto is slices of fresh buffalo mozzarella layered with thin slices of prosciutto crudo, dressed with extra-virgin olive oil and black pepper. It is a classic Italian antipasto that requires no cooking: the mozzarella must be at room temperature and the prosciutto freshly sliced.
sourceNotes: The combination of fresh mozzarella and prosciutto crudo is a staple antipasto throughout southern and central Italy. Mozzarella di bufala originates in Campania and the combination with prosciutto from Parma or San Daniele represents a pairing of two of Italy's most celebrated products.

content.text: Mozzarella di bufala con prosciutto needs two things: mozzarella at room temperature and good-quality prosciutto sliced fresh from the counter rather than from a vacuum pack. Cold mozzarella has no flavour; cold prosciutto loses its silkiness. The rest of the dish is assembly: slices laid on a plate, dressed with oil and pepper, and served with bread.
Remove the {{mozzarella-di-bufala}} from its liquid and bring to room temperature for 30 minutes. Drain well and tear or slice into 6 to 8 pieces each.
Drape {{prosciutto}} of prosciutto slices over a serving plate, folding them loosely rather than lying them flat. Tuck the mozzarella pieces in among the prosciutto.

Drizzle {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} of extra-virgin olive oil over everything. Grind {{black-pepper}} of black pepper on top. Tear over {{basil}} of basil leaves if using. Serve immediately with bread.

items.cause: It was served cold from the fridge.
items.fix: Remove the mozzarella from the fridge 30 minutes before serving. Cold suppresses the mild, milky flavour of fresh cheese.

items.symptom: The prosciutto is sticky and clumped together
items.cause: Vacuum-packed prosciutto tends to stick and does not fan out properly.
items.fix: Separate each slice carefully; they should be very thin. Ask the deli counter to slice fresh if possible , counter-sliced prosciutto stays in separate, silky sheets.

content.text: Mozzarella con prosciutto is one of the simplest and most widely served antipasto combinations in Italian restaurants. It brings together two Italian ingredients: buffalo mozzarella from Campania and cured prosciutto from Emilia-Romagna or Friuli. No sauce, no acid, and no cooking are needed. The fat and salt of the prosciutto contrast with the mild, milky freshness of the cheese, and the olive oil ties them together.
